support.passage: We introduce the Evaluator Stress Test (EST), an invariance-based framework that detects proxy gaming by separating exploitable sensitivity (e.g., format, physics bugs) from content-driven improvements using controlled perturbations with semantic validity audits.

rows.limitations: Max-min correlation formulations depend on specified correlation bounds and linear feature availability. Invariance-based stress testing requires domain-specific perturbation design and cannot guarantee detection of all forms of proxy gaming.
rows.next_questions: Can these robustness guarantees be extended to non-linear feature spaces, and how do they scale to large-scale generative models?
rows.reason: Revision incorporating new confirmatory evidence for robust policy optimization.
rows.summary: Autonomous systems can mitigate reward hacking by combining robust max-min policy optimization over correlated proxy spaces with invariance-based stress testing that isolates exploitable sensitivities from genuine performance gains.
